chapters.title: In hortō
chapters.story: A small Līvia sits under a large tree in the garden.
chapters.editor_note: Preserve the existing first-chapter setting and illustration; audit advanced forms already in the draft.

chapters.title: Familia
chapters.story: The four family members are introduced at their villa.
chapters.editor_note: Keep Mārcus, Flāvia, Līvia, and Tītus consistent in every later scene.

chapters.title: Dōnum
chapters.story: Līvia gives her mother a red rose, while Tītus holds a book.
chapters.editor_note: The red rose must be immediately recognizable in the image.

chapters.title: Cēna
chapters.story: At dinner the family points to bread, water, and cups.
chapters.editor_note: Also include a short review vignette using Chapters I–IV only.

chapters.title: Forum
chapters.story: Mārcus buys two apples and Līvia sees three at a market stall.
chapters.editor_note: Display exactly two bought apples and three on the stall.

chapters.title: Canis
chapters.story: The dog runs along the Roman street towards Līvia at the gate.
chapters.editor_note: Retain the current dog chapter theme; use fair comprehension questions.

chapters.title: Tempestās
chapters.story: In the present tense the family watches clouds, wind and rain.
chapters.editor_note: Replace the overloaded past-tense story with present-time narration.

chapters.title: Vesper — Recēnsiō I
chapters.story: At evening the dog returns home as the family remembers the market visit.
chapters.editor_note: Dedicated illustrated review story with only previously introduced forms.

chapters.title: Herī
chapters.story: A yellow sun today contrasts with the grey storm yesterday.
chapters.editor_note: A two-panel before/now illustration clarifies time.

chapters.title: Sub tēctō
chapters.story: Tītus was reading and Flāvia was working while rain continued.
chapters.editor_note: Contrast ongoing past action with present actions.

chapters.title: Nōlī timēre
chapters.story: Flāvia tells frightened Tītus not to fear the thunder.
chapters.editor_note: Keep this command separate from the new past-tense lessons.

chapters.title: Post tempestātem — Recēnsiō II
chapters.story: The family orders pictures and retells the storm.
chapters.editor_note: Sequence the events with Latin-only picture prompts.

chapters.title: Crās
chapters.story: Līvia prepares roses for a future visit to a friend.
chapters.editor_note: Reintroduce the original Chapter VIII future material gradually.

chapters.title: Iter crāstinum
chapters.story: The family discusses what they will do and hear on the road.
chapters.editor_note: Show how this future differs from -b- verbs, with repeated examples.

chapters.title: Ad amīcum
chapters.story: Mārcus says who will go to the friend's house.
chapters.grammar_focus: Irregular future of īre: ībō / ībimus
chapters.editor_note: Keep other irregular futures out of the initial exposure.

chapters.title: Dōnum amīcō — Recēnsiō III
chapters.story: The family makes the journey and delivers the gift.
chapters.editor_note: Optional repeated reading with an attached verified recording.

chapters.title: In viā novā
chapters.story: A traveller sees a person, dog, river and city.
chapters.editor_note: Formalize canis / canem using high-frequency forms.

chapters.title: Hic an ille?
chapters.story: Līvia distinguishes a near basket from another basket.
chapters.grammar_focus: Demonstratives ille / illa / illud versus hic
chapters.editor_note: The image must show two visibly distinct referents.

chapters.title: Quī venit?
chapters.story: A visitor who lives nearby returns a missing book.
chapters.grammar_focus: Relative clause introduced by quī / quae / quod
chapters.editor_note: Restrict the first exposure to one simple clause position.

chapters.title: Cuius liber? — Recēnsiō IV
chapters.story: The children work out who owns and brought a book.
chapters.editor_note: No passive forms yet; title is only a story label to review before use.

chapters.title: Epistula
chapters.story: Līvia writes about gifts she prepared and a friend she called.
chapters.editor_note: Contrast finished actions with ongoing past scenes.

chapters.title: Nūntius dīxit
chapters.story: A messenger tells the family what he saw, said and did.
chapters.editor_note: Introduce only a few very common irregular perfect stems.

chapters.title: Anteā
chapters.story: The family reconstructs what had happened before the messenger arrived.
chapters.editor_note: Use a two-event timeline; avoid introducing a new subordinate mood.

chapters.title: Quid accidit? — Recēnsiō V
chapters.story: The children reconstruct the events of a missing letter.
chapters.editor_note: Use story sequencing and Latin comprehension questions.

chapters.title: Cum redierit
chapters.story: Mārcus predicts what will happen after Tītus has returned.
chapters.grammar_focus: Future perfect indicative in future-time clauses
chapters.editor_note: Make future completion explicit before more advanced subordination.

chapters.title: Vocātur
chapters.story: At the forum, a messenger describes who is summoned and what is sold.
chapters.editor_note: Compare active and passive with two unmistakable illustrations.

chapters.title: Dōnum repertum est
chapters.story: A lost gift is found and returned to the family.
chapters.editor_note: Teach the compound verb before participles used as adjectives.

chapters.title: In forō — Recēnsiō VI
chapters.story: A market story mixes current, completed and passive events.
chapters.editor_note: Only previously introduced grammatical forms.

chapters.title: Canis currēns
chapters.story: The dog runs after a boy carrying a basket.
chapters.editor_note: Show simultaneous actions in a clear illustration.

chapters.title: Litterae scrīptae
chapters.story: Līvia finds a written letter and an opened box.
chapters.editor_note: Contrast with the perfect passive verbal construction in XXVII.

chapters.title: Ut videat
chapters.story: Mārcus opens a door so that Līvia may see a room.
chapters.grammar_focus: Affirmative purpose clause: ut + present subjunctive
chapters.editor_note: Introduce only this basic use of the subjunctive.

chapters.title: Quid Līvia facit? — Recēnsiō VII
chapters.story: The family practices actions, purposes and descriptions.
chapters.editor_note: Include context cards, a short reread and a teacher-print page.

chapters.title: Manūs et portūs
chapters.story: At a harbour people load goods onto a ship by hand.
chapters.editor_note: Start with natural contrasts rather than an entire declension table.

chapters.title: Diēs et rēs
chapters.story: At a family gathering a problem is resolved as the day goes on.
chapters.editor_note: Keep the story familiar while introducing the forms.

chapters.title: Fābula prīma — Pōns ad librōs
chapters.story: An entirely original animal tale leads into graded independent prose.
chapters.grammar_focus: No new grammar; cumulative bridge story
chapters.editor_note: Only known grammar; suggest public-domain reading after checking provenance.

vocab_note: Sample seeds, not a full 800–1200-lemma course list. Manual review is required.
note: Historical audit only; the active user instruction limits new vocabulary to about 15 words per teaching chapter across about 50 chapters.
